column6: The pour and the head of foam; she is judging whether it behaves like the soda it is replacing.
A nail on the tab and five grams of sugar in a roundel; the number is the permission to open it.
Callouts arrowed onto the can; she reads a drink the way she reads a wrapper.
Shirley Temple staged with real cherries; the flavour is borrowing a drink she already has a memory of.
Cherry cola shot close enough to be abstract; the colour field is the whole creative.
A man in a suit and a tornado simulator; the ad is a bit, and the drink is the price of admission.
Cans staged on the kettlebell rack; the drink is being placed inside a session she already runs.
An outfit flatlay with the can among the jewellery; the pick-me-up is being styled as an accessory.
Parenting is an extreme sport, played straight in a wrecked kitchen; the exhaustion is the targeting.
Less sugar and available at Amazon in the same breath; the claim and the shelf arrive together.
The easy-drinking energy drink with zero grams; the whole category is being repositioned as hard work.
Filmed at the wheel mid-sentence; the car is where the pick-me-up is actually needed.
Two grams against thirty-nine, ten calories against a hundred and forty; the table does the arguing.
Don't be scared, it's just water; the brand is making a joke of its own packaging to defuse it.
A gloved hand and a location tag on a mountain; the can is proof of where somebody stood.
A cookware set on white with no copy; the colour is the only decision left in the funnel.
One word and a hand stirring; the food release from the surface is the entire proof.
The same set again weeks later; the tile is doing catalogue duty rather than making a case.
